summary: An informational memo registering the text/css media type, used to label Cascading Style Sheets so that browsers and other software know how to treat them.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo records the text/css label for Cascading Style Sheets. That label helps software identify an external CSS file when it is fetched.

questions: what is the text/css media type
what is the text css media type
subtitle: The registration details for the text/css media type used by CSS style sheets.

tldr.problem: CSS had been used with the text/css media type without registration, and this memo sought to regularize that use.
tldr.mechanism: It records text/css registration details, including the optional charset parameter and encoding considerations.
tldr.outcome: The RFC provides information about the media type; it does not specify an Internet standard.

today: RFC 2318 is an Informational memo about the text/css media type. The unit metadata lists no later update or replacement.

sections.title: Cascading Style Sheets
sections.content:
Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) describe how structured documents are presented, including fonts, colors, and spacing. The RFC says CSS style sheets may be external files linked to a document or internal content within a document's STYLE element.

CSS had been used with the media type text/css since October 1995 without registration. This memo provides information about that media type.
sections.plainLanguage: CSS contains rules for how a document looks. A style sheet can be a separate file or can appear inside a document.

sections.title: The text/css Media Type
sections.content:
The registration names the type text and subtype css. No parameter is required; charset is optional. CSS syntax is expressed in US-ASCII, but a CSS file may contain strings using Unicode characters.

The RFC says any charset that is a superset of US-ASCII may be used and recommends US-ASCII, iso-8859-X, and utf-8. For transports that are not 8-bit clean, it recommends quoted-printable encoding.
sections.plainLanguage: The registered type is text/css, and it may include an optional character-set label. The RFC recommends quoted-printable for transports that cannot safely carry eight-bit data.

sections.title: Security and Interoperability
sections.content:
The RFC says style sheets contain declarative property and value pairs, not executable code. However, a style sheet can hide information by making text very small or turning off elements.

CSS can also link to other media, and software typically follows those links automatically. The security considerations for each linked file depend on its own media type.
sections.plainLanguage: CSS rules can hide parts of a page even though they are not executable code. A style sheet can also point to other files that software may fetch automatically.
